# Daviana

> Daviana is one connected system that runs a whole hair salon: the appointment diary and till, an AI receptionist that answers the phone and books into that diary, colour formulation weighed and costed to the gram, a drink to the chair, and the app the team opens daily for takings and pay. Five products that read and write the same shared record, so the diary, the colour bowl and the till all agree.

Built and run every day inside six working salons from London to Saudi Arabia, with partner salons across five countries. Not adapted from generic appointment software — written on the salon floor.

## Products
- [Daviana Booking, also called Daviana Diary](https://daviana.app/diary/): the salon booking system and booking spine — appointment diary, till, client records, per-stylist pricing, rota and online booking. Every other product reads and writes this one shared record.
- [Daviana Aria (AI Receptionist)](https://daviana.app/ai-receptionist/): an AI receptionist for hair salons. Answers the salon phone, books into the real diary, answers questions and is straight about price. Catches the calls that ring out when the desk is busy.
- [Daviana ColorLab](https://daviana.app/colorlab/): hair colour management software. Colour weighed on a connected scale, costed to the gram, and written to the client record so the next stylist sees the actual formula used.
- [Daviana Bar](https://daviana.app/bar/): a drink to the chair — posts to the client's bill and deducts stock, instantly, without leaving the floor.
- [Daviana Performance](https://daviana.app/performance/): the app the team opens daily — live revenue and leaderboards, commission and self-employed settlement, tips and gamified training.

- [More tools](https://daviana.app/other-software/): team performance, the salon bar and the free calculators, in one place.

## Key facts
- 19,949 colour formulas weighed and costed to date.
- Running inside 6 salons, London to Saudi Arabia; partner salons in 5 countries.
- Products share one record — booking a client in the diary is the same record the colour and the till read.
- A live demonstration line anyone can ring, no signup: +44 7460 096908.
- Demos are 20 minutes on the phone, run on the salon's own numbers. Ask for one at https://daviana.app/demo/

## Pricing
- [Pricing](https://daviana.app/pricing/): priced per product — Daviana Diary £80 a month, the AI Receptionist £60 a month, ColorLab £80 a month. Bar and Performance are included free once you take the Diary. All prices include VAT. Take one, take all five. No commission on bookings, no per-booking charge, no lock-in, and client lists are never marketed to other salons.
- [Start a free trial](https://daviana.app/trial/): leave a salon name, a mobile and an email; someone rings within one working day and moves the clients, services and prices across by hand. Free for a month, no card.

## Free calculators (no sign-up, nothing stored)
- [Missed call calculator](https://daviana.app/tools/missed-call-calculator/): what a salon's unanswered calls are worth over a year. Every assumption is adjustable.
- [Colour cost calculator](https://daviana.app/tools/colour-cost-calculator/): true colour cost per head, and what it is as a share of the colour service price.

- [What is the best salon software in the UK?](https://daviana.app/blog/best-salon-software-uk/): Fresha, Treatwell, Booksy, Timely, SalonIQ, Phorest and Daviana compared for UK hair, nail and beauty salons: real prices, contracts and new-client fees.
- [What is the best booking system for a nail salon in the UK?](https://daviana.app/blog/best-booking-system-nail-salon-uk/): How to choose a booking system for a UK nail salon: treatment times, technicians, deposits and fees; Fresha, Booksy, Treatwell, Timely and Daviana compared.
- [How many salon phone calls go unanswered? What 1,844 real calls show](https://daviana.app/blog/salon-missed-calls-data/): Real data from a London salon group's phone line: half of calls went unanswered before an AI receptionist, the worst hours and days, and what callers did next.
- [How should a UK salon structure stylist commission?](https://daviana.app/blog/salon-commission-structure/): The three commission structures UK salons use, a worked example to run on your own takings, and the minimum wage and holiday pay rules to check.
- [What should a salon no-show policy say? A UK template you can copy](https://daviana.app/blog/salon-no-show-policy/): A copyable no-show and late cancellation policy for UK salons, with a deposit worked example, the fairness rules to follow, and how to enforce it.
- [Screening stylist applicants without spending a week reading CVs](https://daviana.app/blog/screening-stylist-applicants/): Applications arrive all week and get read on Sunday night, by which point the best candidates have taken another job. A faster way to screen.
- [Why is salon stock always going missing? Back bar control that works](https://daviana.app/blog/salon-stock-going-missing/): Most salon stock isn't stolen, it's unrecorded use. Back bar and retail need separate counting rhythms — not one annual stock take that explains nothing.
- [12 questions to ask before switching salon software](https://daviana.app/blog/questions-before-switching-salon-software/): Twelve honest questions to ask any salon software provider before you switch, covering your data, the changeover, per-stylist cost, and how to leave.
- [Live commission tracking: why stylists shouldn't wait for payday to see their numbers](https://daviana.app/blog/live-commission-tracking/): When commission is only visible on payday, every payslip is a possible argument. Live numbers on the real diary remove the argument before it starts.
- [How much hair colour is your salon really wasting?](https://daviana.app/blog/hair-colour-waste/): Overmixed hair colour goes down the plughole with no record it ever existed. Here's why that happens, and what changes once you weigh the bowl.
- [Why colour formulas get lost when a stylist leaves](https://daviana.app/blog/colour-formulas-when-stylist-leaves/): A client's colour formula usually lives in a stylist's head or a paper card. When that stylist moves on, here is what actually happens to the record.
- [Colour cost per gram: the number most salons don't know](https://daviana.app/blog/colour-cost-per-gram/): Most salons price colour by the tube and guess the rest. Weighing the bowl to the gram shows what a head of colour actually costs — and where the money goes down the plughole.
- [One diary, one till, one client record: what all-in-one salon software actually means](https://daviana.app/blog/all-in-one-salon-software-meaning/): Most salon software sold as all-in-one is several tools behind one login, each with its own copy of the client. Here is the test that shows the difference.
- [Can an AI answer your salon's phone and still book into the real diary?](https://daviana.app/blog/ai-receptionist-real-diary/): How Daviana's AI Receptionist books straight into the real Daviana Diary, and why that stops the double-bookings a bolted-on phone service can't.
- [After-hours salon calls: what happens when nobody's on the desk](https://daviana.app/blog/after-hours-salon-calls/): The salon phone keeps ringing after closing, on Sundays, and when the desk is already busy. Most of those calls become someone else's booking, not yours.
